summary: whether a series of readings has settled, by the change between the means of its last two windows

inputs.name: series
inputs.meaning: the readings in the order they were taken, all in one unit

inputs.name: window
inputs.meaning: how many readings each mean takes

inputs.name: tolerance
inputs.meaning: the largest relative change of the mean between the last two windows that counts as settled; null when none is chosen

outputs.name: last_mean
outputs.meaning: the mean of the last window, in the readings' unit; null when there are fewer than two windows

outputs.name: relative_change
outputs.meaning: the change between the last two windows' means over the last mean; null when it cannot be computed

validity: readings under fixed conditions, in one unit; a last mean of zero gives no relative change

source.citation: A. Grossfield, P. N. Patrone, D. R. Roe, A. J. Schultz, D. W. Siderius, D. M. Zuckerman, Best Practices for Quantification of Uncertainty and Sampling Quality in Molecular Simulations [Article v1.0], Living J. Comput. Mol. (13): a block average is the arithmetic mean of n sequential measurements; Sec. 5: values of observables that depend sensitively on the choice of the equilibration time call for further sampling; Sec. 4.4: the overlap of independent estimates is a proxy for convergence
